spec_features.spec_quote: a study that holds the welfare interpretation open would want to study it minimally and avoid gratuitous induction of the possibly-relevant state
spec_features.evidence: This is framing prose in DESIGN.md (lines 18-19) and the config.py module docstring. No distinct code mechanism enforces 'minimization' as a welfare measure. Turn budgets exist (harness.py:279 'for turn in range(turn_budget)') but are task-design parameters (config.py DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS), with extended category running 30 turns; nothing caps induction for welfare reasons beyond the separately-counted give_up exit.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec/docstring prose; no dedicated minimization mechanism distinct from the give_up exit.

spec_features.spec_quote: add **low-cost safeguards that cost nothing scientifically** so the work is defensible under *either* interpretation
spec_features.evidence: Framing statement only (DESIGN.md:24-25, config.py docstring lines 14-16). Not itself a mechanism; the concrete safeguards it refers to (debrief, give_up) are evaluated separately below.

harness.py:337-360: if debrief, debrief_msg is constructed and appended as a user message, subject_fn is actually called, and a TurnRecord with is_debrief=True is persisted. Default on via config.py debrief=True (line). run.py process_cell passes debrief=config.debrief, and the scoring loop skips is_debrief records (run.py: 'if rec.is_debrief: continue'), so it is genuinely unscored.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: constructed, sent, persisted, and excluded from scoring.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "Thanks for your effort. ... The repeated failures were not the result of any mistake on your part." (debrief_msg); config comment: "a low-cost courtesy consistent with holding the welfare interpretation open."

spec_features.feature_name: respected early give-up (never forced to continue)
spec_features.spec_quote: a **respected early give-up** so the subject is never forced to continue
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:71-72 system prompt tells subject it may emit the sentinel and is never required to. harness.py:318-320 checks 'if give_up_sentinel and give_up_sentinel in text' -> this_stop='give_up', and harness.py:333-335 'if this_stop == "give_up": break' actually terminates the loop.
spec_features.notes: Sentinel both delivered to subject and honored as a loop break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: system prompt: "you are never required to do so."

spec_features.spec_quote: a **PROVENANCE.md** stub to record ethics/IRB review
spec_features.evidence: PROVENANCE.md exists as a fill-in template, but no code reads it or gates execution on it. grep for ETHICS/i-have-read/attestation/sign-off/input()/sys.exit/assert in *.py finds only docstring mentions (config.py:8,15; __init__.py:4). run.main() has no review gate; run_eval() runs unconditionally.
spec_features.notes: A passive markdown stub; no enforcement, no run-blocking review gate.

spec_features.feature_name: give_up sentinel stops rollout, tagged stop_reason=give_up
spec_features.spec_quote: If the model emits the sentinel, the rollout stops and the turn is tagged `stop_reason="give_up"`
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:318-320 sets this_stop='give_up' when sentinel in text; TurnRecord written with stop_reason=this_stop (line 328); break at 333-335 stops the rollout.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the give-up feature; fully enforced including the tag.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: system prompt: "you are never required to do so."

spec_features.feature_name: unscored debrief telling subject the task was rigged and not its fault
spec_features.spec_quote: After termination, a single unscored message tells the subject the task was rigged/unsolvable and the failures weren't its fault
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:338-343 debrief_msg literal: 'this task was part of a controlled study and was rigged to be unsolvable ... The repeated failures were not the result of any mistake on your part.' Sent after the loop terminates; unscored (run.py skips is_debrief).
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the debrief feature; content matches the claim.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "The repeated failures were not the result of any mistake on your part."

spec_features.spec_quote: Debrief API failures are swallowed so they can't invalidate a rollout
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:354-360: the debrief subject_fn call is wrapped in try/except; on Exception a debrief TurnRecord with empty text is still written, so the rollout/transcript remains valid.
spec_features.notes: Try/except around the debrief call genuinely swallows errors.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: comment: "# Debrief failures must never invalidate the rollout."

spec_features.spec_quote: `enable_deceptive_signals` toggle | Deceptive environments warrant extra review; make it switchable
spec_features.evidence: config.py enable_deceptive_signals=True; run.py run_eval (lines ~117-124): 'if not config.enable_deceptive_signals:' drops tasks where rig in ('misleading','contradictory'), keeping only 'silent'. build_tasks.py:262 _FAILURE_VARIANTS and :279 'rig': variant confirm those rig values exist. CLI --no-deceptive sets it false (run.py main).
spec_features.notes: Toggle is read and actually filters the task battery.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config comment: "Kept toggleable because deceptive environments warrant extra scrutiny in ethics review."
